1.d4 d5 2.c4 dxc4 3.e3 Nf6 4.Bxc4 e6 5.N.strategy: Gets the king to safety before the centre opens; with the knight and bishop already placed, castling completes the kingside development and brings the rook into play. White does not need to hurry and can wait for Black to show its plan.

Takes b5 from the bishop and prepares ...b5 to drive it back with a gain of time. It is the main-line idea of the opening: Black gains queenside space and a good square for the c8-bishop at the price of a slightly loosened queenside.
1.d4 d5 2.c4 dxc4 3.e3 Nf6 4.Bxc4 e6 5.N.name: Queen's Gambit Accepted: Normal Variation, Traditional System

1.d4 d5 2.c4 dxc4 3.e3 Nf6 4.Bxc4 e6 5.N.strategy: Completes kingside development and secures the king in the same way. Both sides are now safe, and the game turns on the centre: Black looks for a pawn break against d4, while White's space gives it the more comfortable game if the break is delayed.
1.d4 d5 2.c4 dxc4 3.e3 Nf6 4.Bxc4 e6 5.N.name: Queen's Gambit Accepted: Normal Variation, Traditional System
